Cloud API only (On-Premises sunset 2025-10-23). Three tools: whatsapp.window (read) and whatsapp.templates (read) plus whatsapp.send (write, approval). The block is a boundary rather than a feature, because the PRD's own rule makes our approval pattern a legal constraint: with the 24-hour service window closed a free-form message is NEVER delivered (error 131047) and the customer is left waiting while the agent believes it replied. So 131047 is unreachable BY DESIGN, not caught: the window is computed from our clock and the last inbound timestamp so the answer can be shown to an operator, and a free-form send outside it is refused BEFORE any provider I/O -- measured by scripts/probe_whatsapp_window.py, which shows a closed window refused with ZERO provider POSTs while a declared template still sends, because a template is the only path Meta permits. A template is operator configuration: the model selects one by key and can supply neither the language nor the category, since reclassifying marketing as utility is how an account loses its quality rating, and there is no tool to create or submit one at all. Every recipient is operator-declared (a model-supplied number is an unbounded send surface) and one contact per call, so no broadcast path exists. The two Meta credentials stay in separate keys: messaging sends, management inspects, and a send reads only its own. A timestamp without a timezone is refused rather than read as UTC, because Uzbekistan is UTC+5 and a five-hour error places a send outside the window. A fixed defect of this block, present since P1: engine._submit hardcoded its outbound-tool set ({'telegram.send','instagram.send'}), so every newly registered outbound tool silently lost the engine-level allowed_recipients check -- whatsapp.send was uncovered until this block replaced the literal with named constants and a per-channel destination field. 52 local tests plus the probe and config/whatsapp.example.json. Open: throughput queueing for the 80 msg/s per-number limit, tier/limit observation and a UI. PRD section 2.5 in full: upload -> parse -> normalize -> validate -> duplicate check -> PO/delivery matching (3-way) -> exception and fraud controls -> approval routing -> payment and ERP sync planning -> mock ERP post -> audit log. Five tools: document.parse (write), document.match / document.duplicates / document.fraud_signals (read), document.posting_plan (write, approval). The platform DOES NOT MOVE MONEY: there is no pay step anywhere, and the furthest the chain goes is a posting plan, which is a proposal. That claim is tested from three independent directions rather than asserted -- syntactically (16 public callables checked against a 13-term money vocabulary), through the registry at EVERY ladder (5 tools x 3 ladders = 15 cells, all with 0 provider calls, INCLUDING autonomous where no human approves the step), and in the output (the plan carries executes_payment=False and says so in a sentence a human can quote). Money is an integer count of minor units; a float is refused outright because binary floating point cannot hold every decimal amount exactly and a check off by one tiyin is a check nobody should trust, and a submitted amount is truncated rather than rounded so the number later compared is not inflated. A document that disagrees with itself is refused before any check runs: line items must sum to the stated total, and an ambiguous date such as 10.01.2026 is refused rather than guessed because guessing shifts a duplicate window by months. The duplicate key is (kind, supplier, number) and deliberately EXCLUDES the amount: the same number with a different amount is more suspicious than an exact repeat, not less, and a re-submitted number never overwrites the stored original because the original is the evidence of what was first seen. The three-way match keeps absent evidence and contradicting evidence apart (incomplete vs mismatch), because collapsing them sends an approver looking for something that is not there; with no tolerance declared the required agreement is exact, since a non-zero default would silently excuse mismatches the operator never agreed to excuse, and two currencies are never compared without a rate. Fraud controls report SIGNALS WITH EVIDENCE and never a verdict, split into material signals that hold a posting (duplicate_altered, amount_outlier, bank_account_changed) and weak ones that are reported without gating (round_number, weekend_date, no_history): most legitimate invoices are round, so gating on that would train an approver to click through the warning. THE DEFECT OF THIS BLOCK, and it was silent: the tools declared fields as a bare {"type": "object"} schema, and the registry validator rejects every nested dict that has no declared properties ("Schema fields mismatch"), so all five tools refused EVERY call at the engine boundary. They were registered, referenced by the capability packs, with the correct risk -- and unsubmittable. No registration test can catch that; the probe did, because it submits through a real Engine. Fixed by carrying structured arguments as JSON text with one decoder (_payload), since a document is a tree and cannot be flattened without losing its shape; 3 regression tests lock it, including one that asserts the broken shape is still rejected. Also fixed: weak signals used to gate the plan, so a clean matched round invoice was held; and weekend_date made a claim it had not checked. 84 local tests plus the probe and config/documents.example.json. Migration note: engine.py p_migrations now has version 8, which correctly broke two tests that asserted [1..7]; they were updated, not deleted. Open: real ERP sync (this block stops at mock ERP post), an OCR/extraction layer (deliberately absent: fields arrive already extracted, because quietly guessing at a scanned amount is worse than refusing it), a UI, and live acceptance NOT_RUN.

A manager question routes to the right section agent. The whole design follows one rule: the supervisor's authority is never inherited (PRD v0.5 section 4, UPA). Routing is a routing decision, not a permission grant -- the target's own policy is re-resolved through AgentLoop.create, and the supervisor's tools, allowed_connections, ladder and allowed_recipients are never copied, merged or widened. The security property is measured rather than claimed: scripts/probe_supervisor_authority.py shows a supervisor holding no data tool routing to an agent that holds connectors.read, and proves both that the supervisor's policy is byte-identical afterwards and that the target is refused when it attempts a tool its own policy lacks. Authority flows to the executor, not to the asker. Chains are bounded three ways: max_hops (default 1) is counted from the ledger so a restart cannot reset it, a section whose agent is itself a router is refused by default so supervisor->supervisor is unreachable, and run creation lives in the control plane rather than in a registered tool so no agent can manufacture delegated runs by naming one. An unmatched question is refused by name rather than sent to a default agent. Routing is deterministic keyword matching (longest wins, then declaration order), deliberately not a model decision, because a route that cannot be explained cannot be audited. Two read tools (supervisor.route reports the map and creates no run; supervisor.sections). 53 local tests. Multi-hop chains, a section statistics endpoint and a UI remain.

Hierarchical asset model over the business graph, derived from the operator's own register: the path IS the identity (zavod-1/sex-2/liniya-3/stanok-7) and the register's id column is that path, so no second numeric asset_id is minted. The operator declares the levels; the code only validates their count and name legality, so a different customer can declare a different hierarchy with no code change. Read-only by design: there is no write path anywhere in the module, because an entity that can edit the model would be the author of the identity every event, measurement and report depends on -- the platform reads the customer's UNS, it does not own it. Five read tools (asset.levels, asset.tree, asset.children, asset.descendants, asset.resolve). The sharpest property is that descendants are compared BY SEGMENT, never by string prefix: 'zavod-10'.startswith('zavod-1') is True, so a naive prefix test would let one plant's query return another plant's assets -- and it would do so silently. Two path rules are deliberately two functions: parse_path requires exactly the full depth (identity) while prefix_path accepts any depth up to it (navigation: children, descendants, subtree bounding), because a shared flag would let an identity call drift into the prefix rule. A fixed defect of this block: business_graph.preflight only gated allowed_connections for connectors.read/database.read, so every sheets-backed source was unchecked since P1 -- a source reaches a connection either by naming it in args or, for sheets, through its register, and both are now resolved before any provider I/O. 56 local tests plus 2 regression guards in the graph suite. Does not read SCADA, does not manage cameras (that is P11b), does not read measurements: it only makes assets exist so that a camera event or a cycle time has something to bind to. Tree UI, a measurement time series and per-asset maintenance history remain.

Camera events as one more bounded read source. Frames NEVER reach the platform: only {station, event, timestamp, confidence} is read, and this is a legal requirement rather than an optimisation, because under Uzbekistan Law No. O'RQ-1125 (26.03.2026) biometric data must stay local and be entered in a state register. Three read tools, split in two classes as the PRD requires: vision.station_event (impersonal: defect, cycle time, idle, SOP deviation) and vision.person_event (person-identifying, i.e. BIOMETRIC, human_led mandatory). The gate is a hard refusal that runs before any provider I/O, so an agent with the wrong ladder cannot cause I/O against biometric data at all -- measured, not claimed, by scripts/probe_vision_biometric_gate.py, which shows autonomous and human_assisted refused with ZERO GETs and only human_led reading. The identifying-class vocabulary is TENANT-WIDE, not per-register: a class is a property of the event, not of the sheet it happens to sit in, so a face-detection row landing in the shop-floor sheet is still dropped by the impersonal read. vision.summary never counts person events, since a count of identified people is itself biometric processing, and it is explicitly not an OEE figure (that needs cycle times and planned run time: P13). Each event binds to an ASSET (a leaf path) so it can appear on that asset's graph.timeline; an event naming an intern node is reported in 'unbound' rather than attached to a node the customer never asked about. Reads are windowed (ISO since/until) and bounded, because the stream is continuous in reality. Confidence is reported verbatim and never turned into a correctness claim. 48 local tests plus the probe. Open: a webhook ingest point, event dedup, a UI. Also OPEN and unfixed, recorded here deliberately: sheets.py reads an empty allowed_connections as 'everything permitted' while the rest of the runtime reads it as 'nothing permitted' (see V05G section 4.2).

OEE, andon and the pipeline that feeds them, and the two refusals that shape the whole block. P12 refused OEE by name and handed it here ('availability and performance need planned run time and ideal cycle time, which no register there declares'); this block honours that handover. Two read tools (oee.report / oee.andon) and no write path at all, because an entity able to edit a run time would be the author of the OEE it reports on. Three factors, each computed ONLY from declared inputs and each refused by name when its inputs are absent -- never defaulted, never assumed: availability = run/planned, performance = (ideal*produced)/run, quality = good/produced. The single most important property is that a partial OEE is never a number: if any factor is uncomputable, oee is null and not_computable names exactly which inputs are absent or unusable, because an index assembled from one measured factor and two defaults looks complete and is not. absence and unusability are reported separately (a produced count of zero divides by zero; a good count above produced is a data error -- reporting it would give an OEE of 347%), so the operator is sent to the right fix. Planned run time and ideal cycle time are DECLARATIONS, not measurements, so they are declared as a column or as a per-station constant; when both are declared the column wins and the constant fills in for a blank cell, an unreadable non-blank cell uses neither, and declaring both is accepted configuration rather than the ambiguity that two REGISTERS would be. Availability is not clamped to 100% when run exceeds plan and performance is not floored to 1.0 when the line runs below standard, because both are facts and clamping either hides a defect behind a perfect number. andon is the DETECTION half only: it returns which station crossed which declared threshold with the measured value and the bound, the fact and not the verdict, and delivery reuses the P6 escalation coordinator rather than growing a second notification path. Thresholds are operator configuration, so the platform does not decide that 85% is a bad OEE, and with none declared andon refuses by name instead of inventing a bound; a station whose OEE is uncomputable is counted as not_evaluated and raises NO breach, so a missing column name never pages a manager about a failing line. No person is evaluated, structurally: an OEE attributed to a machine is a maintenance signal, the same number attributed to the operator on that shift is a sanction. Every read goes through sheets.rows, so the register declaration, A1 allowlist, agent tool permission and connection allowlist apply unchanged. The boundary is measured, not described: scripts/probe_oee_boundary.py holds 78 measured properties across seven sections (the seventh measures the post-implementation ultra-audit fixes), and it caught the defect class this block is most exposed to -- documentation that contradicts the code. The header claimed two declared plan sources would be REFUSED; measurement showed the column wins and the constant is the blank-cell fallback, a coherent design the docs denied and my own example, checker and tests had encoded wrongly. The probe was fixed to measure the rule, the refusal boundary was pinned to two registers, and three tests were added. The post-implementation ultra-audit found and fixed five more real defects in this family, all of them silent: a non-finite cell (inf/nan) read as a number in BOTH oee._number and manufacturing._number, where inf >= 0 is true so an infinite run time accumulated into a factor that no downstream guard catches; a CRITICAL blind spot in andon, which inherited the caller display limit from report and so evaluated only the stations it returned while hard-coding complete: True -- a breaching station past the limit was silently skipped and a plant on fire reported breach_count: 0; an opaque not_evaluated that was a bare count where not_computable had already established that the missing metric must be NAMED (now not_evaluated_metrics and not_evaluated_stations); and a latent off-by-one in the BOM truncated flag that reported True at exactly MAX_BOM_LINES having dropped nothing. The BOM defect is unreachable in situ because sheets.MAX_ROWS caps the source at 200 and raising max_rows above 200 is itself refused, so its regression test lowers the ceiling instead of trying to exceed it -- latent does not mean absent, only currently silent. andon now evaluates every station (limit only bounds what is RETURNED), complete is derived from the read rather than asserted, and the note states in Uzbek that a truncated list is not complete. The alarm must see every station the read saw, because truncation is a harmless caveat on a report and a hole in an alarm.

Inventory read block, local-contract tested. PRD v0.4 P4 and the customer's own words -- 'sotuvchi narxni olib yurmasin', the seller must not carry the price around -- answered the OTHER way round from the tracker's own note: no typed MoySklad adapter was needed, because the Business Graph already reads MoySklad through connectors.read and already resolves which system disagrees. A second reader with its own source list would have been a second answer to the same question. So the block adds NO transport, NO connection and NO register: api-python/platform_runtime/inventory.py declares four read tools (inventory.product / inventory.stock / inventory.price / inventory.margin) that name an ENTITY and a ROLE->attribute mapping, and every read goes through business_graph.resolve(), so the register declaration, A1 allowlist, agent tool permission and connection allowlist all apply unchanged. Seven boundaries, each measured rather than described by scripts/probe_inventory_boundary.py (68 properties over 6 sections): a price always ships the source that produced it, because a number with no provenance is a number a salesperson cannot defend; a conflict is reported and under the default 'report' policy NOTHING is selected, which is the PRD's own rule that both numbers are legitimate (the accountant knows the 1C number, the seller knows the MoySklad number); blank, zero and unread are three different facts and nan/inf are refused rather than sailing through as readable; a margin is computed ONLY from two readable inputs; stock is a quantity and is NEVER translated into available, because the platform does not know about reservations, quarantine or a warehouse the register does not track; nothing is attributed to a person; and there is no write path in the file at all -- a price is master data and an entity able to edit the price it reports on would be the author of the number a salesperson quotes. FIVE real defects were found in this block by audit rather than by use. Three of them were found in a later audit phase, after the ASCII-cell sweep, by reading the reason vocabulary rather than the arithmetic: _reason() had no name for a declared priority that selects an unreadable cell while another source holds a readable value, so the tool returned price_reason=unread and no price at all even though ERP held the number -- and sending the operator to repair the source that was fine instead of the priority line that was wrong. The case was shown reachable by measuring business_graph._view, which sets selected on a conflict under primary_wins. price() also returned different key sets on its two paths: the single-product branch carried name and currency but not price_reason, which is the exact field the tool's own note tells the reader to consult, while the catalogue branch carried price_reason but not the names. And the new fifth reason was filed under not_computable by both product() and margin(), because each split on a hardcoded reason != 'conflict', so a fixable configuration line was reported as missing data; POLICY_REASONS is now a module constant used at all four call sites. test_inventory.py grew 38 -> 82 and probe_inventory_boundary.py 68 -> 141 properties, with a new section measuring that the five reasons partition every state into exactly one bucket. The earlier two defects were found in this block BY ITS OWN TESTS before it shipped: report-policy conflict made a margin silently None, which reads as 'cannot compute' when the truth is 'will not choose', so the output now splits not_computable (missing or unusable data) from margin_blocked_by_conflict (a policy refusal) because the two send an operator to two different places; and the single-product path returned margin_reasons while the catalogue path returned not_computable, an inconsistent key. 38 tests plus the probe, plus config/inventory.example.json and scripts/check_inventory_example.py which validates the example against the module's OWN validator and found two real inconsistencies in the example (category and currency were mapped but not produced by the graph). Fixes the silent source_priority drop in business_graph: the key was whitelisted, so an operator was told it existed, and then read by nobody -- graph_config returned only conflict_policy and entities, so every consumer was blind to it. PRD 6.3 per-attribute priority now works, a priority naming an undeclared source or an unmapped attribute is refused instead of becoming a silent no-op, explain() names the order that chose a value, and an omitted entity priority is now deterministic instead of depending on JSON key order. Open: a UI, and MoySklad live acceptance (live_verified stays False).

Owner-configured daily digest. Source is the Business Graph (graph.search / graph.conflicts), so every source authority is checked before any provider I/O and every value keeps the system that produced it. Delivery is read plus notify: the only write is telegram.send, which addresses the operator and never a customer, so no approval is required — hiding a briefing behind an approval would train operators to approve reflexively. The delivery half of workforce oversight (P9b detects overdue work and stops there). A scheduled coordinator reads overdue rows through the ordinary workforce.workload handler — so the register declaration, A1 allowlist, agent tool permission and connection allowlist all apply unchanged and this module adds no new data path — and notifies the manager once per work item. Two read tools (escalation.preview / escalation.schedules); delivering is a coordinator action, not a tool, so a model cannot manufacture a manager message and the dedup/cooldown cap is enforced by code rather than by a prompt. The module crosses no evaluation line: no score, rank, rating or productivity figure exists anywhere in it (PRD v0.5 section 8), the digest names the person, task, due date and status as facts, and every message states in text that the platform does not evaluate the employee and takes no disciplinary decision. The dedup key is (tenant, schedule, person, task, due) — the work item, not the person — and a sent row is terminal for that key permanently, so one late task produces one escalation however many cycles run; a task rescheduled to a new due date is a new key and is escalated again on its own merits. Only an undelivered row (a crashed claim, or a provider failure past its cooldown) is ever retried. An unread register is never rendered as 'nothing overdue': the cycle sends nothing, audits the exception class only, and reschedules rather than retiring the loop. The recipient is operator configuration, must be pack-allowlisted for the agent at configure time, and provider text cannot redirect it. An item too old to keep escalating (max_age_days) is counted and carried into the next real escalation rather than sent alone, so a permanently-late task leaves a trace without becoming an hourly nag. Authority and freeze are re-checked every cycle, and a revoked owner disables the schedule with an auditable reason. 45 local tests plus scripts/probe_escalation_boundary.py. A UI, a per-item acknowledgement and live Telegram acceptance remain.

Closes the highest-severity finding of the P8c audit: whatsapp_inbound recorded the 24-hour window the customer opens and nothing read it. whatsapp.send now resolves the window from two sources in named precedence -- window_sources returns (resolved, sources, status) and a VERIFIED INBOUND EVENT WINS OUTRIGHT over the operator register, which is not the same rule as 'the newer of the two', because a register a human hand-edited cannot reopen a window Meta's own timestamp says is shut, and the two sources can legitimately disagree. The event stream is read from p_events through the engine's own read path (no new store), newest-first, bounded by MAX_EVENTS_SCANNED, tenant-scoped by the query itself. The sharpest defect of the block was found by the probe, not by the tests: whatsapp_inbound stores window_until as the EXPIRY (Meta timestamp + 24h) while window_state takes the LAST INBOUND TIME and adds the 24 hours itself, so passing the stored value straight through added them twice and a customer who wrote 25 hours ago read as open -- precisely the 131047 condition the module exists to prevent. Fixed by converting back: float(stamp) - WINDOW_SECONDS, with a regression test that fails against the unconverted form. window() rows now carry a 'source' field so an operator can see which source answered instead of a bare boolean. whatsapp was deliberately NOT added to engine.OUTBOUND_CHANNELS: (a) the window and the destination answer two different questions; (b) adding it would MOVE whatsapp.send from the allowlist branch to the event-binding branch, which is a rule swap and not an addition; (c) a template send legitimately happens outside the window and has no event to bind to. 65 new tests (test_whatsapp.py 54 -> 119) plus scripts/probe_whatsapp_window_sources.py. Open: a UI and live Meta acceptance.

PRD v0.5 section 2.8 proposes wa_window_until as a new attribute on the Business Graph customer entity. Investigated against the real modules and REFUSED; see docs/development/V05-BLOCKS-MESSAGING-UZ.md. The reason is mechanical rather than a matter of taste: a graph attribute IS a provider row column, because _collect reads row.get(field) for every mapped attribute, so declaring it would mean the window lives in a cell a human types. A hand-typed cell does not refresh when the customer writes, so the platform would replace a fact it verified itself (the Meta-signed message the inbound block recorded) with one it did not -- the same defect P8c shipped and P8d closed, one layer down. Deriving it from the graph read time is also refused: observed is our local read time, not the provider update time, and a briefing and a send reading different snapshots would disagree about one customer. Making whatsapp.window a graph source was considered and rejected too: SAFE_SOURCE_TOOLS is limited to the four row-returning read tools, whatsapp.window answers from the tenant config rather than from entity_id so an id could not be bound to a contact without a second declaration, its payload is not a row list, and it would need three permissions for a question it already answers alone. The PRD goal is met: whatsapp.window returns open, closes_at and source (event or register) and is the same resolver the send gate consults before any provider I/O. So no attribute is added; instead 6 guard methods (WaLifecycleGuardTests, 52 collected tests because they inherit every existing graph fixture) in test_business_graph.py fail if one ever appears, and scripts/probe_wa_window_graph_attribute.py measures the four reasons independently. No new tool: build_registry()=69.

The step after document.posting_plan, which ended at a proposal. This block writes to the customer's ERP, and it is the most dangerous code in the repository, so three properties are enforced rather than documented and each is measured by scripts/probe_erp_posting_boundary.py. (1) Money is still never moved: a posting creates an accounting document -- a payable -- and paying it stays a human act in the ERP the customer already trusts. The claim is narrower than the document block's so it is measured separately: no public callable in the module carries a money-moving name, and posting_body() is the complete set of values the module can send. (2) An incomplete document is refused BY NAME and never completed: seven fields are required, five from the documented and two (account, counterparty) from the operator's register as ALIASES, because a model that could name a raw account code could mispost a debt on a one-digit slip. A missing field joins a 'missing' list; a malformed one is raised immediately with its own reason, because 'we could not read the amount' and 'the amount is not a number' send an operator to different places. The two operator fields are keyword-only and are never read from the document, so an attacker-influenced invoice cannot choose where its own debt lands. (3) Posted at most once, guarded three ways plus a fourth: the ERP search (find_posted, which FAILS CLOSED -- not being able to ask is not the answer being no), the local ledger checked BEFORE any I/O, and a UNIQUE index on a claim_key that survives a race; and a failed attempt stays retryable, because the first draft put the UNIQUE index on (tenant,driver,kind,supplier,number) so a transport blip made a legitimate invoice permanently unpostable. Only statuses that ASSERT the ERP holds the document (posted, skipped_existing) occupy the index. A 2xx with no document identifier is recorded as unconfirmed, not posted. Both drivers are exercised, not just one: custom_http differs from onec_http only in how the answer is READ (a flat id vs result.Ref_Key), and that difference is measured, because a driver that changed nothing would let a custom ERP fail to see a document it already holds -- the double-posting condition. erp.posting_submit is deliberately NOT in engine.OUTBOUND_TOOLS: that gate answers 'may this agent address this recipient' and a posting has no recipient; its guard is the document identity, which the ledger and the ERP search already enforce before any I/O. BOM, cycle time and yield over the asset model. The PRD lists four things Jidoka's cameras feed into an ERP (OEE availability/performance, SOP deviation events, cycle time per unit, quality alert flags) and this block turns THREE of them into numbers while refusing the fourth. The refusal is the point and it is enforced in code, not described: OEE availability and performance need planned run time and ideal cycle time, which no register here declares, so vision.summary's refusal ('bu P13 ishi') is kept rather than an availability figure invented from whatever happens to be present. Three read tools (manufacturing.bom / manufacturing.cycle / manufacturing.yield) and no write path at all, because a BOM is the customer's master data: an entity able to edit what a product is made of would be the author of the recipe it reports on, and every yield and cycle figure would then be computed against a model it could change. Cycle ships a mean with its sample count and unreadable count beside it, and a measured cycle with no declared standard is reported as measured and marked compared:false rather than judged fast or slow -- calling it slow would mean the platform invented the baseline. Yield is computed only when both output and defects are readable; where they are not, the station ships yield:null and yield_computable:false rather than assuming zero defects and printing 100% for a line that might be rejecting half its work, and a defect count above output is reported rather than clamped because it is a data error the manager must see. A blank cell and a confident zero are different facts: both are counted through separate unreadable counters and neither becomes zero, and a row with no readable output produces no station at all. No per-person figure exists and no config key could create one -- a yield attributed to a person is a sanction waiting for a reason the platform does not have. Stations bind to the P11 asset hierarchy by segment, never by string prefix, so zavod-1 can never claim zavod-10's output, and an unbound station is reported without a path plus an unbound count rather than attached to a guessed node. Every read goes through the ordinary sheets.rows handler, so the register declaration, A1 allowlist, agent tool permission and connection allowlist all apply unchanged. STAGE A (done, LOCAL_CONTRACT_TESTED): call events plus a hard consent gate. Three read tools -- telephony.consent, telephony.call_events, telephony.summary -- and no dialer at all, because placing a call is an outbound write to a person and the consent gate must be enforced by code on the one path that can reach a provider, not by a prompt on a path any agent could hold. Two tools would have been enough for reporting; consent is a third because "may we call this number, and may we record it" is a question a caller must be able to ASK without being able to ACT, so a missing record yields consented: false WITH A REASON rather than an exception -- and a MALFORMED record raises at configure time, because a typo must never read as granted. Audio never reaches the platform, enforced structurally rather than promised: no tool argument, config key or output field carries a recording, a URL, a transcript or a buffer, the module imports no audio surface at all, and a locator-shaped cell (scheme-prefixed URL or a media extension such as .wav/.mp3/.opus) is WITHHELD and counted in withheld_outcomes rather than republished as a call outcome -- the defect the probe caught, because "treat the column as opaque text" is exactly how a recording link leaks into a model context and from there to a third party. The filter is deliberately narrow: an ordinary outcome word survives. A number is one number: every comparison goes through digit normalisation and exact equality, never a prefix, because the same segment-not-prefix discipline P11 applies to asset paths applies here to phone numbers and a prefix match would call a stranger because a shorter number was consented. Purpose is declared PER REGISTER and is a closed vocabulary (service, delivery, payment, support, marketing); it is never read from a column, because a row that could relabel itself could relabel a marketing call as a service call to pass the gate, and a delivery consent is not a marketing consent. Recording requires its OWN consent: absent permission reports recording_allowed: false and is never read as evidence that no recording exists. An outbound row naming an unconsented number is not hidden and not shown as a normal call -- it carries consent: false with the reasons and is counted in refused_without_consent. No person is evaluated: no per-agent count, rank, rating or leaderboard, because a count of calls is a fact about a telephone line while a count per agent is a number that will be used in a review. Every read goes through sheets.rows, so the register declaration, A1 allowlist, agent tool permission and connection allowlist all apply unchanged. 54 tests, a 7-section probe with 63 measured properties (which caught the locator leak), config/telephony.example.json plus a checker and an ops.telephony capability agent (registry 79 -> 82). STAGE B (done, LOCAL_CONTRACT_TESTED): the outbound queue, the throughput ceiling and the retention window. TWO more read tools -- telephony.queue and telephony.retention -- and still no dialer, because the queue names what COULD be called and the retention view names what SHOULD be destroyed, and both acts belong to an operator with a lawful basis rather than to the platform. The queue lists only outbound rows: an inbound call is never a queue item because we did not choose to make it, so there is nothing to schedule and no pace to respect. A row whose consent check fails is LISTED, not hidden, with consented: false and its reason, because hiding an ungated row would leave an operator believing their list is clean. The throughput ceiling is ENFORCED and not merely reported: a tenant declares per_window calls per window_seconds, and if the read finds more callable rows than the pace could carry the surplus is counted in over_capacity and is NOT presented as callable -- an overstated queue is worse than a short one, because the remedy for a short list is to wait and the remedy for an overstated list is nothing. An ABSENT pace is the safe default and means ZERO capacity, so an operator who has not decided their pace has not decided to call anyone. limit bounds the ITEMS CARRIED and never the evaluation, so matched and over_capacity describe the whole window and a caller given only a slice cannot pace against the wrong number. Retention is a REPORT and never an act: retention_days is REQUIRED whenever a consent register is declared (VO-07 makes retention an operator obligation, so omitting it is an incomplete declaration rather than a default) and must be finite, the platform never deletes a call record, deleted is always 0, and every row lands in exactly one of in_window / past_window / unaged -- with unaged deliberately NOT folded into either of the others, because a row whose date cannot be read must never be expired by accident on a typo. The stage's own audit caught a real defect: queue() called consent() per outbound row and consent() re-read the consent register each time, so a fifty-row queue cost fifty provider GETs -- correct results, no failing test, and a hidden O(N) amplification that would have broken the provider's rate limit as the queue grew. Fixed with an internal _index seam (one read passed into consent(), never exposed on the tool surface, so a single question about one number still gets a fresh read); the probe now MEASURES that a 60-row queue costs the same hops as a 12-row one. 24 new tests that run on the SAME engine and fixtures as stage A by subclassing its test class, so a stage-B change that broke a stage-A invariant fails a stage-A test. open_risks: expiry-boundary sweep in the app layer (2026-09-20): applied the phase-nine rule (a boundary test must sit ON the boundary) to the auth layer, where a clock error is a security matter rather than a correctness one. identity_store has 15 raw time.time() reads, the densest in app/, and four expiry readers: _invitation, validate_session and rotate_session all refuse with expires <= now while list_sessions accepts with expires > now. Measured that the two are exact complements at every instant, and that equality resolves as expired -- the safe direction for an access boundary -- so the CODE is correct. The finding is again in the guard: test_invitation_expired_rejected sets expires=1, which is epoch second 1, about 57 years in the past. Both <= and < refuse that, so the test passes whichever predicate is in force and measures nothing about where the bound sits -- the same shape as the limit=99 mistake in phase nine, now repeated in a different layer. Only equality discriminates. Added four tests using a frozen clock, each asserting BOTH sides so it cannot pass by refusing everything: invitation at expires==now refused and one second earlier accepted; the same bound on validate_session; the same bound on rotate_session (using two separate sessions, because a rotation refused for expiry deliberately revokes the whole token family before raising so a rollback cannot resurrect descendants, which would poison a retry); and list_sessions, which must be the exact complement of the gate so an operator never sees a live session the platform will not honour. Guard-revert: all four predicates flipped (<= to <, > to >=) give 4 failures in test_identity_hardening, and the old expires=1 test stays green, proving it measured nothing. test_identity_hardening 27 -> 31; probe grew 173 -> 181 properties with section 15. Two of my own probe expectations were wrong and the measurement corrected them: expires = now - 1 does NOT separate <= from < (both refuse), so equality is the only discriminating position; and a guard-detection check that matched one literal line reported a missing guard that was present, so it now counts occurrences instead.

clock-consistency sweep (2026-09-20): the engine takes an injectable clock (Engine(..., clock=...)) and it is not decoration -- deadlines, leases, approval expiry and escalation windows all read it -- but the WhatsApp SEND GATE called window_state(last) with no now, so it silently fell back to time.time(), a clock the platform does not control. Measured by moving ONLY the engine clock ten windows into the future and leaving the wall clock alone: the gate sent anyway. The consequence is not theoretical, because the clock is a public interface: a test with an injected clock cannot pin the answer, a replay gets a different one, and two hosts with skewed clocks disagree -- and this is precisely the module built to prevent Meta's 131047, where a message refused as 'window closed' never reaches the customer. Fixed with _engine_now(engine), which reads the engine clock and falls back to the wall clock only for a bare stub, and by passing it at both production call sites; window_state itself was NOT changed, because its now=None default is correct for a caller asking a pure question -- the defect was at the call site. The most valuable part is that two tests were PINNING the defect: they seeded an inbound event at time.time() - (WINDOW + 60) while the engine clock starts at RECENT, captured at import, and the measured import-to-now drift is 60.0s against a 60s test margin. They passed only because the gate ignored the engine clock, and fixing the code broke them; they now anchor on self.clock.now so the fixture and the answer share one clock. test_whatsapp 119 -> 120. Swept the whole class: escalation, usage_budget, workforce and whatsapp now all read the engine clock, and no module has an undeclared raw wall-clock read (whatsapp keeps exactly one, the default of its own fallback). Probe grew 159 -> 173 properties with section 14; note the probe's FIRST version called _engine_now directly and passed on the reverted code too, because it measured the HELPER rather than the CALL SITE -- it now reads the send function's source for a bare window_state(last), which turns the revert red (2 FAIL). Guard-revert: the new test fails with 'Forbidden not raised', the whatsapp suites show 1 failure and nothing else.

exception-type sweep (2026-09-20): the API layer's call() mapper turns six exception types into status codes (RateLimited->429, Forbidden/AuthenticationError->403, NotFound->404, Conflict->409, ValueError/LookupError->422) and TypeError is not one of them, so a guard that refuses a caller's mistake with TypeError reports a 500 -- the caller gets blamed for nothing and the operator is paged. Swept all 867 raise sites (26 distinct types, ValueError dominant at 477) and all 53 routes; 15 routes bypass the shared mapper, and measurement showed none of them raise (the four ledgers and list_tasks clamp, sync_ledger accepts any policy id), so no live 500 exists today. One outlier: engine.list_tasks('t','x') raised TypeError from min(200,max(1,limit)); verified by AST across the whole repo that list_tasks is called only with the tenant, so it is unreachable today -- a latent trap, not a live defect. Hardened anyway to match the runtime's own ValueError convention, and because the day /tasks grows a limit query parameter it would answer 500 where every other bounded reader answers 422. Note the two ends of a clamp are two different decisions: 500 clamps down to the ceiling (200), 0 and -5 clamp up to the floor (1), because a page of zero rows is never what a caller meant; and bool is an int subclass, so limit=True silently became a page of 1 and had to be refused by name. test_engine 55 -> 57 (an arbitrary non-integer raises ValueError, an out-of-range integer is clamped not refused, each end asserted separately); probe grew 143 -> 159 properties with section 13. lease-bound complementarity sweep (2026-09-20): a claimed step's ownership token carries a lease, and two separate methods ask whether it is still alive. They sit in different methods, are written as different literals, and are tied together by nothing -- yet their safety property is that they are EXACT COMPLEMENTS: at every instant, equality included, exactly one fires. That property breaks silently in two directions. If the sweep were strict (`lease < now`) then at equality NEITHER fires and the step is stranded `running` under a dead claim with nothing to retire it -- measured directly, the row stayed status='running' with its claim token intact after a second worker's claim attempt. If finish were inclusive (`lease >= now`) then at equality BOTH fire and a worker can report a step the sweep has already retired as `uncertain`. The pre-existing test_stale_claim_cannot_finish advances the clock by 91 against a 90-second lease -- one second PAST the bound, where both forms agree -- so it measured that a stale lease is refused and nothing about where staleness begins. Probe section 17 added (193 -> 213 properties; 2 FAIL on revert, 0 on restore).
